prompt: What is a single bond?

choices.text: A bond in which one electron pair is shared between the two atoms
A bond in which one electron is shared
choices.why: Every covalent bond shares a pair of electrons. A single bond shares one pair.

choices.text: A bond formed only by a π overlap
choices.why: A single bond is a σ bond. π bonds appear in double and triple bonds.

choices.text: A bond between two different elements
choices.why: A single bond can join any two atoms, including two carbons, as in ethane.

explanation: The bonds in methane and ethane are called single bonds because they result from the sharing of one electron pair between bonded atoms.

prompt: How many electrons are shared in a carbon–carbon double bond?
explanation: A double bond shares two electron pairs: the two electrons of the sp2–sp2 σ bond and the two of the 2p–2p π bond, four in all.

prompt: Which orbitals combine to form sp2 hybrid orbitals?

choices.text: The 2s orbital and two of the three 2p orbitals
The 2s orbital and all three 2p orbitals
choices.why: That combination gives sp3 hybrids.

choices.text: Two 2s orbitals and one 2p orbital
choices.why: There is only one 2s orbital; sp2 means one s and two p.

choices.text: The 2s orbital and one 2p orbital
choices.why: That gives sp hybrids.

explanation: If the 2s orbital combines with only two of the three available 2p orbitals, three sp2 hybrid orbitals result and one 2p orbital remains unchanged.

prompt: How many sp2 hybrid orbitals does an sp2-hybridized carbon have?
explanation: Combining one 2s and two 2p orbitals gives three sp2 hybrid orbitals; the third 2p orbital is left unhybridized.

prompt: What is the angle between two sp2 hybrid orbitals, in degrees?
explanation: The three sp2 orbitals lie in a plane at angles of 120° to one another.

prompt: Where is the unhybridized p orbital on an sp2-hybridized carbon?

choices.text: Perpendicular to the plane of the three sp2 orbitals
In the same plane as the sp2 orbitals, between two of them
choices.why: The leftover p orbital is at 90° to the sp2 plane.

choices.text: It points directly away from one of the sp2 orbitals
choices.why: It sticks up and down, perpendicular to the sp2 plane.

choices.text: There is none; all the p orbitals are hybridized
choices.why: Only two of the three p orbitals are used; one stays unhybridized.

explanation: The three sp2 orbitals lie in a plane at 120° to one another, with the remaining p orbital perpendicular to the sp2 plane.

prompt: What two bonds make up the carbon–carbon double bond in ethylene?

choices.text: One σ bond from sp2–sp2 overlap and one π bond from 2p–2p overlap
Two σ bonds from sp2–sp2 overlap
choices.why: One part is a σ bond, but the other comes from sideways overlap of the unhybridized p orbitals: a π bond.

choices.text: Two π bonds from 2p–2p overlap
choices.why: A double bond has one σ bond and one π bond. Two π bonds plus a σ bond make a triple bond.

choices.text: One σ bond from sp3–sp3 overlap and one π bond
choices.why: The carbons in ethylene are sp2, not sp3.

explanation: Two sp2 carbons form a strong σ bond by sp2–sp2 head-on overlap, while their unhybridized p orbitals overlap sideways to form a π bond. Together they share four electrons in a double bond.

prompt: How is a pi (π) bond formed?

choices.text: By sideways overlap of two unhybridized p orbitals
By head-on overlap of two hybrid orbitals
choices.why: Head-on overlap gives a σ bond.

choices.text: By overlap of an s orbital and a p orbital
choices.why: A π bond comes from two p orbitals side by side.

choices.text: By transfer of electrons between p orbitals
choices.why: A π bond shares electrons in overlapping p orbitals.

explanation: When two sp2 carbons approach each other, their unhybridized p orbitals interact by sideways overlap to form what is called a pi (π) bond.

prompt: Where are the electrons of a π bond found?

choices.text: In regions above and below the line drawn between the nuclei
Centered on the line between the nuclei
choices.why: That describes the electrons in a σ bond.

choices.text: Only on one of the two carbons
choices.why: The π electrons are shared by both carbons, in lobes above and below the bond axis.

choices.text: In the sp2 hybrid orbitals
choices.why: π electrons are in the overlapping unhybridized p orbitals.

explanation: The electrons in the σ bond occupy the region centered between the nuclei, while the electrons in the π bond occupy regions above and below a line drawn between the nuclei.

prompt: What is the overall shape of an ethylene molecule, H2C=CH2?

choices.text: Planar, with bond angles of about 120°
Tetrahedral at each carbon, with 109.5° angles
choices.why: Ethylene's carbons are sp2, so the molecule is flat with angles near 120°.

choices.text: Linear, with 180° angles
choices.why: Linear geometry goes with sp carbons, as in acetylene.

choices.text: Bent, with 90° angles
choices.why: The sp2 carbons give angles near 120°, all in one plane.

explanation: Four hydrogens form σ bonds with the remaining four sp2 orbitals, so ethylene has a planar structure with H–C–H and H–C–C bond angles of about 120°.

prompt: What is the measured H–C–H bond angle in ethylene, in degrees?
explanation: Ethylene's bond angles are approximately 120°. The actual values are 117.4° for H–C–H and 121.3° for H–C–C.

prompt: What is the C=C bond length in ethylene, in picometers?
explanation: Ethylene has a C=C bond length of 134 pm, shorter than the 153 pm C–C single bond in ethane.

prompt: What is the strength of the C=C bond in ethylene, in kJ/mol?
explanation: The C=C bond in ethylene has a strength of 728 kJ/mol (174 kcal/mol), compared with 377 kJ/mol for the C–C bond in ethane.

prompt: Why is a carbon–carbon double bond less than twice as strong as a single bond?

choices.text: The sideways overlap in the π bond is not as great as the head-on overlap in the σ bond
A double bond shares fewer electrons than two single bonds
choices.why: A double bond shares four electrons, the same as two single bonds. The difference lies in how well the orbitals overlap.

choices.text: The two carbons are farther apart in a double bond
choices.why: A double bond is shorter (134 pm) than a single bond (153 pm).

choices.text: Double bonds are made of two π bonds
choices.why: A double bond is one σ bond plus one π bond.

explanation: The double bond is shorter and stronger than a single bond because it has four bonding electrons, but it is less than twice as strong (728 versus 377 kJ/mol) because sideways π overlap is weaker than head-on σ overlap.

prompt: How much stronger is the C=C bond in ethylene (728 kJ/mol) than the C–C bond in ethane (377 kJ/mol), in kJ/mol?
explanation: 728 kJ/mol − 377 kJ/mol = 351 kJ/mol. That is less than another full single bond (377 kJ/mol), because the π part of a double bond overlaps less well than the σ part.

prompt: How many σ bonds does an ethylene molecule, H2C=CH2, contain?
explanation: There are four C–H σ bonds (each from an sp2 orbital and a hydrogen 1s orbital) plus the C–C σ bond from sp2–sp2 overlap: 5 in all. The double bond's second part is a π bond.

prompt: Formaldehyde, CH2O, contains a carbon–oxygen double bond. How is its carbon hybridized?

choices.text: sp2
sp3
choices.why: sp3 carbons form four single bonds. A carbon in a double bond is sp2.

choices.text: sp
choices.why: sp carbons are found in triple bonds (or two double bonds), as in acetylene.

choices.text: It is not hybridized
choices.why: Like the carbons in ethylene, a carbon in a double bond uses sp2 hybrid orbitals.

explanation: Hydrogen forms one bond, carbon four and oxygen two, so the only arrangement is H2C=O. Like the carbons in ethylene, the carbon in formaldehyde is in a double bond, so its orbitals are sp2-hybridized.

prompt: In propene, CH3CH=CH2, how are the carbons hybridized?

choices.text: The CH3 carbon is sp3, and the two double-bond carbons are sp2
All three carbons are sp2
choices.why: The CH3 carbon has only single bonds, so it is sp3.

choices.text: All three carbons are sp3
choices.why: The two carbons in the double bond are sp2.

choices.text: The CH3 carbon is sp2, and the double-bond carbons are sp3
choices.why: It's the other way round: double-bond carbons are sp2, and the CH3 carbon is sp3.

explanation: In propene the CH3 carbon has four single bonds and is sp3; the two double-bond carbons are sp2. The C=C–C and C=C–H angles are about 120°, and the other angles are near 109°.

prompt: How many of the carbons in 1,3-butadiene, H2C=CH–CH=CH2, are sp2-hybridized?
explanation: Every carbon in 1,3-butadiene is part of a double bond, so all four are sp2, and all the bond angles are near 120°.

prompt: What value would you predict for the C=C–C bond angle in propene, CH3CH=CH2, in degrees?
explanation: The middle carbon is sp2, so the angles around it, including C=C–C, are approximately 120°.
